title: “Why Are Your Posts So Long?”
paragraphs:
“Why Are Your Posts So Long?”
Because Jesus Never Told Me to Feed His Sheep Snack-Sized Truth
“Simon, son of John, do you love Me?”
The question pierced deeper than any sword.
Not because Peter did not know the answer.
But because Jesus already knew the failure.
And hidden inside that restoration was a command that still echoes across centuries.

Βόσκε τὰ ἀρνία μου
(Boske ta arnia mou)

Ποίμαινε τὰ πρόβατά μου
(Poimaine ta probata mou)

Βόσκε τὰ πρόβατά μου
(Boske ta probata mou)
Feed them with the Word of God.
Feed them with what nourishes the soul.
And that is why many people ask me:
“You would get more likes if they were shorter.”
“You would have more followers if you simplified everything.”
Perhaps shorter content would attract more clicks.
Perhaps fewer words would create more engagement.
Perhaps more entertainment would create more visibility.
But I was never called to chase algorithms.
I was called to feed sheep.
The modern world often wants spiritual snacks.
But starving souls do not need snacks.

Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἄρτος τῆς ζωῆς
(Egō eimi ho artos tēs zōēs)
And real spiritual growth requires more than thirty seconds of attention.
The truth is many believers today know Christian slogans but not Christian doctrine.
They know church traditions but not Scripture.
They know denominational positions but have never personally examined the Word of God.
They know what others say about Jesus.
But they do not know Jesus deeply for themselves.
Because eternity is too important for shallow understanding.
The Gospel is not simple because it is small.
The Gospel is simple because it is true.
The Apostle Paul spent entire letters explaining salvation.
The writer of Hebrews spent chapters explaining Christ's priesthood.
Luke wrote one of the longest books in the New Testament.
Moses wrote entire books detailing God's covenant.
Jesus Himself often preached messages that lasted long enough for people to become hungry.
The Kingdom has always required attention.
And salvation itself required a cross.
Many ministries measure success by numbers.
When crowds left because His teachings became difficult, Jesus did not dilute the truth to win them back.

“Do you want to go away as well?”
(John 6:67)
Jesus was never interested in gathering crowds at the expense of truth.
And dead hearts need more than motivational content.
The Hebrew Scriptures describe God's Word as:

“Your word is a lamp to my feet.”
(Psalm 119:105)
But darkness does not disappear because someone flashes a light for three seconds.
Darkness is overcome by remaining in the light.
This is why I continue writing what many would consider “too long.”
Because somewhere there is a broken husband searching for answers.
Somewhere there is a wife praying through tears.
Somewhere there is a prodigal son sitting in guilt.
Somewhere there is a young believer trying to understand grace.
Somewhere there is an atheist secretly reading.
Somewhere there is a wounded Christian who nearly gave up on God.
Somewhere there is a soul standing one step away from surrendering to Christ.
If even one person encounters Jesus through these words, then every paragraph is worth it.
Every hour spent writing is worth it.
Every prayer poured into these articles is worth it.
Because one soul is worth more than all the applause this world can offer.
The Gospel has never been about convenience.
It has always been about surrender.
So if these articles are longer than what social media prefers, I make no apology.
Because my goal has never been virality.
My goal has always been faithfulness.
I am praying that the Holy Spirit guides every article to the exact person who needs it.
The one wondering whether God could ever forgive them.
Because the entire Gospel can be summarized in four words:
The Bible is one continuous story of scandal transformed by grace.
And at the center of every story stands Jesus Christ.
The Savior who specializes in rewriting ruined stories.
The cross proves that God is not searching for perfect people.
That means your failure is not the end.
Your addiction is not the end.
Your shame is not the end.
Your past is not the end.
Your scandal is not the end.
Not because numbers matter, but because souls matter.
Someone may need this reminder today.
Send it privately to a struggling believer.
Let that be your declaration that truth matters more than trends.
Because supporting the spread of the Gospel is not merely consuming content.
It is participating in the mission.
And if these writings have helped feed your soul, helping them reach another soul is one way to glorify God through what He has already used to bless you.
One day, likes will disappear, algorithms will vanish, platforms will fade, and every earthly metric will be forgotten—but every soul touched by the Gospel will matter forever.
